prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee,

I come before you today to address these grave and, frankly, un-American allegations with a clear conscience and a full heart.

Let the record reflect: I have never, in my life, "beaten traffic." Traffic and I have an understanding. We coexist. To suggest I would abandon my team—my *family*—in their hour of need, down by only fourteen points with a full twelve minutes remaining, is an affront to everything this cookout stands for.

*[gestures at the assembled hot dogs]*

I ask you, members of the Committee: Would a man who left early *know* that the concessions ran out of the good buns by halftime? Would he speak so passionately of the third-quarter comeback that *almost* happened? I think not.

Now, I have been asked whether I know any "traffic beaters." And I say to you plainly: I decline to answer on the grounds that my second cousin Reginald did, in fact, leave in the fourth quarter of the '09 playoffs, and I will NOT have my good name dragged into his cowardice.

*[leans into microphone]*

You want a confession? Here is my confession: I stayed until the bitter end. I high-fived strangers. I stood for the singing. And when the lot cleared, yes—I sat in my car for forty-five minutes, engine off, staring into the middle distance, *contemplating my choices.*

That, sir, is not beating traffic. That is patriotism.

I yield the remainder of my time to the potato salad.
